<thought>Based on the mass (≈ 100 Da) the molecular formula is most consistent with C₅H₈O₂. The ¹H NMR shows a 3 H doublet of doublets (2.93 ppm) coupled to a single proton at 4.43 ppm, indicating a CH₃–CH fragment where the CH is attached to an electronegative atom (O). The remaining signals (5.04 ppm, 2 H dd and 6.05 ppm, 1 H ddd) correspond to a terminal alkene (CH₂=CH–) that is coupled to the same CH. The ¹³C NMR shows five carbons: two olefinic carbons (≈ 136 and 117 ppm), an O‑CH₂ carbon (≈ 70 ppm), an O‑CH₃ carbon (≈ 54 ppm), and a methyl carbon (≈ 44 ppm) attached to the O‑CH. This pattern matches the structure of methyl crotonate (CH₃‑CH=CH‑C(=O)‑OCH₃), whose SMILES is `C/C=C/C(=O)OC`. This SMILES satisfies the formula C₅H₈O₂ and is consistent with the observed NMR couplings. 
</thought>
<final_answer>C/C=C/C(=O)OC</final_answer>
